items.title: Tennessee Gov. Officially Proposes Naming Nashville Airport After Dolly Parton
items.summary:
Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee has formally proposed renaming Nashville International Airport in honor of Dolly Parton, announcing the plan Friday in partnership with the airport itself. Lee's office said he spoke with Parton's team before going public, and that they were touched by the idea.

"Dolly Parton's extraordinary life is forever woven into the fabric of our state," Lee said in a statement. "At a place where Tennessee welcomes the world, it is fitting that Nashville International Airport would bear the name of our state's favorite daughter."

The proposal does not rest with the governor alone. As Consequence reported, the Metropolitan Nashville Airport Authority will take up the question at a meeting set for September 17th, and State Rep. Todd Warner has said he intends to introduce legislation to make the change.

The announcement follows a fan-led petition pushing for the renaming, which had gathered more than 150,000 signatures by Friday afternoon. Public sentiment has run strongly toward attaching Parton's name to the airport, known by the code BNA, where much of the state's visitor traffic arrives.

Should the airport authority and legislature both sign off, Nashville International would become the first international commercial airport in the United States named for a woman. For now the proposal is an announced intent, awaiting the September 17th vote.

items.title: Bill Maher Delivers Lamest Dolly Parton Tribute Yet
items.summary:
Bill Maher opened Friday night's episode of his HBO series Real Time with a segment on Dolly Parton's death that drew immediate criticism for its tone, capping a week in which the country and the culture at large marked the singer's passing.

After a short run of material on President Trump's latest dispute with Canada, the 70-year-old comedian turned to the tributes that had accumulated over the week. "All this is going on and all America could really talk about this week was how sad it is that we lost Dolly Parton," Maher said, before running through the memorials: the Santa Monica Ferris wheel lit with hearts, the Empire State Building in pink, London joining in.

He then closed the list with a joke about the Sphere in Las Vegas adding a nipple to its display, followed by "Get it?" — the line Variety singled out in its account of the segment as one of the worst Parton tributes on record.

Parton died this week at 80, following what her team described as a brief battle with cancer. Beyond her standing as a country songwriter and performer, she built the Imagination Library, a literacy program that has put books in the hands of millions of children worldwide.

The reaction to her death has been unusually broad, spanning music, politics and public landmarks on two continents. Maher's segment sits awkwardly against that, and it follows a stretch in which his show has already taken heat — last week he devoted airtime to defending Natalie Harp, and he has faced questions over his own recent media appearances alongside figures including Hunter Biden.

items.title: Anne Hathaway Joins Tom Cruise in ‘Days of Thunder’ Follow-Up; Paramount Sets Release Date (EXCLUSIVE)
items.summary:
Anne Hathaway will co-star with Tom Cruise in Paramount's continuation of Days of Thunder, and the studio has set the film for release on June 2, 2028. Variety reported the casting and the date exclusively, and Cruise marked the news himself on Saturday by posting a promotional image of the two of them on a NASCAR track.

Cruise returns as Cole Trickle, the driver he played in Tony Scott's 1990 original. Hathaway will play a racecar team owner and engineer. Jonathan Levine, who directed Long Shot, is attached to helm, with Cruise producing alongside Jerry Bruckheimer and Tommy Harper. Plot specifics remain undisclosed.

Paramount is shooting the film for IMAX and plans an exclusive theatrical release across premium formats including Dolby Cinema and 4DX. The 2028 date lands nearly four decades after the original, which paired Cruise with Robert Duvall as a retired racing veteran and also featured Nicole Kidman, Randy Quaid and John C. Reilly.

For Cruise, the project is his first major franchise commitment since winding down Mission: Impossible. He remains attached to another Top Gun installment and will appear in Alejandro González Iñárritu's drama Digger this year.

Hathaway arrives with an unusually crowded slate. She has had four films in theaters in 2026 — Mother Mary, The Devil Wears Prada 2, The Odyssey and The End of Oak Street — with the Colleen Hoover adaptation Verity still to come. She recently wrapped the military drama Alone at Dawn opposite Adam Driver and is developing a third Princess Diaries film for Disney.

items.title: Ella Langley Covers “Jolene” in Tribute to Dolly Parton
items.summary:
Ella Langley covered "Jolene" during her Friday night concert in Auburn, adding her own tribute to the wave of remembrances following Dolly Parton's death. Consequence reported on the performance, which Langley framed for the crowd before playing it.

"Tonight's show didn't feel right without doing something like this," Langley told the audience, according to video from the show, before launching into the song.

She followed the performance with a written tribute on Instagram. "Dolly, thank you for standing up for yourself as an artist, a songwriter, a musician, a producer, an author, a creative, and most importantly, a woman in this industry," Langley wrote.

"You paved the way for so many to be brave," she added. "Thank you for being unafraid to show your most authentic self. The world needed Dolly and will never see another like it. The gates of heaven just welcomed home a beautiful soul."

The Auburn show was one of many stages where Parton's catalog surfaced this week as performers folded her songs into their sets.

items.title: Taylor Swift Donates $50k to Help Mother Struck by Car
items.summary:
Taylor Swift donated $50,000 to a GoFundMe campaign supporting Ashley Taunton, a mother of three who was struck by a car while helping at the scene of an accident. Rolling Stone confirmed the donation, which is intended to cover the family's daily expenses while Taunton recovers.

According to the fundraising page, Taunton pulled over during a heavy rainstorm after spotting someone in need following a crash. "It was just Ashley doing Ashley things," her husband Joe said. While she was assisting, another vehicle hydroplaned toward the scene and Taunton pushed a bystander out of its path before being hit herself.

The page says Taunton has undergone two major surgeries with more scheduled, and faces a long recovery. Swift appears to have left a message in the campaign's comment section reading, "Wishing you the best recovery possible and sending love to your family!"

The donation follows a much larger act of giving earlier this year. Ahead of their July wedding at Madison Square Garden, Swift and her husband, Travis Kelce, distributed $26 million across 20 charities in the United States.

Those recipients were chosen from cities tied to the couple's own histories, among them the Los Angeles Regional Food Bank, The Store in Nashville, Helping Harvest in Swift's hometown of Reading, Pennsylvania, and Children's Mercy Hospital and Harvesters in Kansas City. After-School All-Stars in Kelce's native Cleveland was included, along with national organizations including Feeding America, the ASPCA, Grammy In The Schools and Dolly Parton's Imagination Library.
